elements.element: Preferred: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice
elements.evidence: "PB as Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon 90 days' prior written notice to SFJ"

elements.element: Preferred: pro-rata refund of prepaid fees on Customer convenience termination
elements.evidence: No refund language; instead "an amount not exceeding three (3) months' Development Costs as the sole early-termination fee" is payable by PB

elements.element: Preferred: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term
elements.evidence: "SFJ as Vendor may terminate this Agreement for convenience only effective at the end of the then-current term"

elements.element: Fallback: Customer termination right for convenience exists
elements.evidence: "PB as Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time"; deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present" ok

elements.element: Fallback: Customer notice period within 60–90 days
elements.evidence: "upon 90 days' prior written notice to SFJ"

elements.element: Fallback: early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: "an amount not exceeding three (3) months' Development Costs as the sole early-termination fee" (replacing "three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs")

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor convenience termination only effective at end of a term
elements.evidence: "only effective at the end of the then-current term ...; Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are limited accordingly"

elements.element: Fallback: Vendor convenience termination on 90 days' notice
elements.evidence: "and only upon 90 days' prior written notice to PB"

reasons: All four fallback atomic elements are met: a Customer convenience right, 90 days' notice (within the 60–90 band), an early-termination fee capped at three months' Development Costs, and a Vendor convenience right confined to end-of-term on 90 days' notice.
Preferred fails on two independent elements: notice is 90 rather than 30 days and there is no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, so the clause sits at the locked fallback level only.

Minimality is not fully satisfied: the alias tags "as Customer" and "as Vendor" are unnecessary labelling of already-defined parties, and the trailing sweep "Sections 14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are limited accordingly" reaches beyond convenience termination into the change-of-control and JSC-deadlock exits, which are triggered rights rather than convenience rights.

Intent is preserved on balance: the Trial Data Package purchase mechanic, Approval Payment/Buy-Out adjustments and the Section 14.2.6 payment formula remain effective, and the express "limited accordingly" override avoids a bare contradiction, though it leaves the scope of the limitation on §§14.2.6/14.2.10 somewhat imprecise.

Note for the rationale rather than as a deviation: removal of the $60 million spend gate and the pre-first-approval cut-off expands Customer's exit and benefits our party, so it should not be flagged.
